cards: Shalmaneser III was king of Assyria from 859 to 824 BCE.
Ashurnasirpal II was King of Assyria from 883 to 859 BCE and one of the founders of the Neo-Assyrian Empire.
Ahab was king of Israel in the 9th century BCE, the son of Omri, reigning from Samaria roughly between 871 and 852 BCE.
Omri was king of Israel from about 884 to 873 BCE and founder of a dynasty that included his son Ahab.
reigned c. 884–873 BCE · Ancient Near East
Jezebel was a Phoenician princess, the daughter of Ethbaal, king of the Sidonians, who married King Ahab of Israel in the ninth century BCE.
Elijah was a Hebrew prophet of the 9th century BCE in the northern Kingdom of Israel, known from the biblical Books of Kings.
Hazael was a king of Aram-Damascus who seized the throne around 842 BCE; an Assyrian text calls him the son of a nobody.
r. c. 842–796 BCE · Ancient Near East
Jehu was king of Israel from about 841 to 814 BCE.
reigned c. 841–814 BCE · Ancient Near East
Osorkon I was the second king of the Twenty-second Dynasty of Egypt, son of Shoshenq I, reigning for about 35 years in the late 10th and early 9th centuries BCE.
d. c. 887 BCE · Ancient Near East
Ahaziah was king of Judah for about a year around 842–841 BCE, the son of Jehoram and Athaliah.
d. c. 841 BCE · Ancient Near East
Athaliah was queen of Judah for about six years in the 9th century BCE, the only woman to rule either Hebrew kingdom in her own right.
d. c. 835 BCE · Ancient Near East
Baasha was king of Israel in the early ninth century BCE, reigning about twenty-four years according to the Books of Kings.
early 9th century BCE · Ancient Near East
Elisha was a prophet of the northern Kingdom of Israel in the ninth century BCE, the disciple and successor of Elijah according to the Books of Kings.
Ishpuini was king of Urartu in the late ninth century BCE, the son of Sarduri I.
r. c. 828–810 BCE · Ancient Near East
Jehoram, or Joram, was king of Israel in the mid-ninth century BCE, the son of Ahab and the last king of the House of Omri.
r. c. 852–841 BCE · Ancient Near East
Jehoshaphat was king of Judah in the first half of the 9th century BCE, the son of Asa.
King Xuan of Zhou was the eleventh king of the Western Zhou dynasty, who came to the throne after the Gonghe regency.
Caranus was, according to later Greek writers such as Theopompus and Diodorus, the founder of the Argead royal house of Macedon, a descendant of Heracles from Argos, traditionally dated to the 9th…
Hadad-yith'i was a ruler of Guzana, the Aramaean kingdom of Bit-Bahiani in north-eastern Syria, in the 9th century BCE.
Hadadezer, called Adad-idri in Assyrian records, was a king of Aram-Damascus in the 9th century BCE.
r. c. 865–842 BCE · Ancient Near East
Kapara was a king of Guzana, the Aramaean kingdom of Bit-Bahiani at Tell Halaf in north-eastern Syria, probably in the 10th or 9th century BCE.
c. 10th–9th century BCE · Ancient Near East
King Li of Zhou was the tenth king of the Western Zhou dynasty, reigning from about 877 to 841 BCE.
r. c. 877–841 BCE · Central & East Asia
Marduk-zakir-shumi I was king of Babylon from about 855 to 819 BCE.
r. c. 855–819 BCE · Ancient Near East
Nabu-apla-iddina was king of Babylon from about 888 to 855 BCE, one of the longest reigns of the period.
r. c. 888–855 BCE · Ancient Near East
Osorkon II was a pharaoh of the Libyan Twenty-second Dynasty of Egypt, ruling from Tanis and Bubastis.
r. c. 872–837 BCE · Egypt & North Africa
Pedubast I was a king of Egypt in the late 9th century BCE, usually counted as the founder of the Twenty-third Dynasty.
Takelot II was a king of the Libyan period of Egypt in the second half of the 9th century BCE, usually placed in the Twenty-second Dynasty.
Arame was the first known king of Urartu, ruling in the mid-ninth century BCE.
Jehoahaz was king of Israel in the late 9th century BCE, the son of Jehu.
Jehoiada was a priest in Jerusalem in the 9th century BCE who, according to the Bible, led the coup that overthrew Queen Athaliah.
Jehoram was king of Judah in the mid-9th century BCE, the son of Jehoshaphat.
